quotes.text: That is the reframe this whole episode is built around. PCF is not decoration. It is the enforcement layer.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the episode's central thesis in one line.

quotes.text: Citizen developers are not the risk. A business analyst dragging a field onto a form is not what causes a tenant to buckle. Ungoverned components are the risk.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Shifts blame from people to missing structure.

quotes.text: PCF without ALM is just custom code with extra steps. That isn't a critique of the framework itself. It's a description of what happens when a team treats PCF as a coding exercise instead of a delivery discipline.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Makes the case that ALM is the backbone of any PCF strategy.

quotes.text: Every PCF component you deploy is a promise. A promise that someone will maintain it. That its performance will be watched. That its dependencies won't quietly rot.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains the long-term cost behind each custom component.

quotes.text: Chaos does not come from non-developers having access. It comes from missing guardrails. Those are two completely different problems and they call for two completely different fixes.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear diagnosis that separates access from guardrails.

takeaways: PCF is not a UI skin but an enforcement layer: once a code component is packaged in a solution it becomes a versioned, traceable dependency that every app inherits.
Use standard controls first and PCF only for structural gaps, and back every component with a governed catalog, ALM pipeline, managed environments and a review process.
Citizen developers are not the risk; missing guardrails are, so a federated model with a central catalog lets business users build safely while leadership funds governance as platform infrastructure.
hook: Many Power Platform tenants drown in undocumented apps, fragile web resources and duplicated grids. This episode is for architects and platform owners who want to see the Power Apps component framework as a governance layer, with solutions, ALM, catalogs and managed environments that let low code scale safely.
